preamble: Lateralization (lambdacism) of /d/ to /l/. In Latin it is sporadic: a handful of words show l- or -l- where cognates have d (lingua, lacrima, olēre), variously explained as Sabine borrowing or folk-etymological influence. In Pashto it is regular: Old Iranian *d became l word-initially and intervocalically, so Pashto las 'ten' and lur 'daughter' correspond to Persian dah and dokhtar.

examples.note: Sporadic d- > l-, explained as borrowing from another Italic language with the shift and/or association with lingō 'to lick'.
Same sporadic d > l; cognate with Greek δάκρυ.
The verb shows l while the noun odor keeps d.

sources: Kreidl, J. (2021). Lambdacism and the Development of Old Iranian *t in Pashto. Iran and the Caucasus. https://doi.org/10.1163/1573384x-20210207
